summary: **Shri Jishnu Barua, Chairperson Shri Ramesh Babu V., Member Shri Harish Dudani, Member Shri Ravinder Singh Dhillon, Member** Approval under Section 62 read with Section 79(1)(d) of the Electricity Act, 2003 and under Regulation 15(1)(a) and Regulation 23 of Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 2023 for determination of the transmission tariff for the 2024-29 tariff period under the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2024 from COD to 31.3.2029 for **“Eastern Region Expansion Scheme - XXXV (ERES-XXXV)” in the Eastern Region.** Power Grid Corporation of India Limited. Katwaria Sarai, New Delhi. 110016. Corporate Centre: ‘Saudamini’, Plot No-2, Sector-29, Gurgaon-122 001 (Haryana). **1. Bihar State Power (Holding) Company Limited** Vidyut Bhawan, Bailey Road, Patna - 781001, Bihar **For Petitioner** : Shri Zafrul Hasan, PGCIL Shri Angaru Naresh Kumar, PGCIL Shri Arjun Malhotra, PGCIL The instant petition has been filed by Power Grid Corporation of India Limited (Power Grid) for determination of tariff under the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2024 (hereinafter referred to as “the 2024 Tariff Regulations”) for the period from COD to 31.3.2029 in respect of the 2. The hearing in this matter was held on 13.10.2026, and the Petition was reserved. 4. The Petitioner has claimed the following annual transmission charges with respect to the transmission asset for the 2024-29 tariff period as under: 5. The Petitioner, through prayer at Sr. No. (p), has requested to allow the interim tariff in accordance with Regulation 10(3) of the 2024 Tariff Regulations, for the purpose of inclusion in the PoC charges. 6. We have considered the Petitioner’s submissions for the grant of an interim tariff. 7. As per Regulation 10(3) of the 2024 Tariff Regulations, the Commission may grant an interim tariff in case of new transmission projects that have filed the application under Regulation 9(1) of the 2024 Tariff Regulations. However, under Regulation 10(3) of the 2024 Tariff Regulations, the Commission may grant an interim tariff up to 90% of the tariff claimed in case of new transmission projects under the aforesaid Regulation. _(3) If the information furnished in the petition is in accordance with these regulations, the Commission may consider granting an interim tariff of up to ninety per cent (90%) of the tariff claimed in the case of a new generating station or unit thereof or transmission system, or element thereof during the first hearing of the application for billing purposes till the final tariff is determined by the Commission:_ _(5) The Commission shall grant the final tariff in the case of existing and new projects after considering the replies received from the respondents and suggestions and objections, if any, received from the general public and any other person permitted by the Commission, including consumers or consumer associations._ _(6) Subject to Sub-Clause (7) below, the difference between the tariff determined in accordance with clauses (3) and (5) above and clauses (4) and (5) above, shall be recovered from or refunded to, 29 the beneficiaries or the long term customers, as the case may be, with simple interest at the rate equal to the 1 year SBI MCLR plus 100 basis points prevailing as on 1st April of the respective year of the tariff period, in a maximum of six equal monthly instalments;_ _Provided further that such interest, including that determined as per sub-clause (7) of this regulation shall be payable till the date of issuance of the Order and no interest shall be allowed or levied during the period of six-monthly instalments. Provided further that in case where money is to be refunded and there is a delay in the raising of bills by the generating company or transmission licensees beyond 45 days from the issuance of the Order, it shall attract a late payment surcharge as applicable in accordance with these regulations._ _(7) Where the capital cost approved by the Commission on the basis of projected additional capital expenditure exceeds the actual trued up additional capital expenditure_ (AFC) claimed by the Petitioner and taking into consideration the time overrun in case of the instant transmission assets, the same shall be discussed and analysed in detail at the time of grant of the final tariff order. Accordingly, the Commission has decided to allow an interim tariff @ 90% of the AFC claimed with respect to the asset for the 202526, 2026-27, 2027-28, 2028-29 tariff periods in terms of Regulation 10(3) of the 2024 Tariff Regulations. 10. Accordingly, we hereby allow the interim annual transmission charges subject to the final tariff order as follows: 11.
